name: DEC Sewage Pollution Right to Know page, 'Recent NY-Alert Notifications' view
waters_covered: statewide; receiving water as typed by the notifier
access_detail: Server-rendered Drupal view (class c-view--sewage-notification) inside the SPRTK page; each row = <li class='c-view__row'> with a headline span, <time datetime='UTC ISO'> and the full NY-Alert message text. No JSON:API (/jsonapi 404), no view RSS, no node links per alert. Fetched 2026-11-01: 1 row (Warwick SD#1 UPDATE issued 10-31-2026 20:59). Wayback snapshots (2025-10-14, 2025-10-15, 2026-01-09, 2026-01-19, 2026-04-17, 2026-05-15) show 1-15 rows each, so the view lists a rolling recent window (page text says 'within the last 7 days'; observed counts suggest a shorter window or row cap). Scraping is possible; page is behind a bot check for some clients (Wayback captured 403 pages several times).

sample_record.headline: UPDATE: Orange, Warwick, Sewage Discharge, Tributary of Longhouse creek,
sample_record.text: New York Sewage Pollution Right to Know UPDATE Issued: 10-31-2026, 20:59:00  Affects: New York - Orange - Warwick The Warwick (T) SD #1 NY0021890, NY0021890 is issuing this notification. Discharge location: 50 State School Rd, Warwick, NY ... Waterbody affected: Tributary of Longhouse creek ... Discharge date and time: 05-30-2025 00:00:00 Discharge duration: unknown Hours  Discharge reason: System Capacity -  Sand filter system not operating correctly ... Volume/rate of discharge: 60,000 Gallons Estimated  Treated state of discharge: Partially Treated with Disinfection ...

fields: headline (UPDATE:/ENDED:/none + county, municipality, 'Sewage Discharge', waterbody, public area)
cannot_fill: outfall id (only sometimes in location details, e.g. 'Kelsey CSO', 'Regulator 013A', 'SSO #005')
revision linkage (no shared id between initial, update and ended)
cadence: rows appear when notifiers file in NY-Alert; observed DEC view time equals NY-Alert 'Issued' time within seconds (some notifiers' Issued is 1 h behind during DST). Legal deadline: public within 4 h of discovery.
history: rolling window only; older alerts only via Wayback snapshots or DEC Excel workbooks
license: No licence statement on the page; DEC site 'Website and Usage Policies' apply (not quoted; https://dec.ny.gov/about/website-usage-and-policies). Data caveats on page: 'Data quality is not checked by DEC.'
status_reason: The only public, no-login web surface carrying full SPRTK alert text in near real time; scrape-able but fragile and without ids.
notes: Compared with the DEC workbook: the headline prefix (UPDATE:/ENDED:) is not reliable; Close and Update notices from several notifiers (Kenmore, Onondaga County, Erie County, Washington County) appear with no prefix. The <time> element matched NY-Alert air time for most notices but ran exactly 1 h late for some (Auburn, Skaneateles, April 2026). The page view is a copy of NY-Alert public messages; notices flagged 'does not reach surface water' are not sent to the public (manual).

name: NY-Alert 'Sewage Discharge Notifications' subscription (email, text, phone, fax)
operator: NYS Division of Homeland Security and Emergency Services (NY-Alert platform, Everbridge back end); alerts authored by municipal notifiers
access_detail: Requires a NY.gov ID account, then NY-Alert (Everbridge member portal https://member.everbridge.net/saml/login/NYAlert/...) subscription: My Subscriptions > Edit > county > check 'Sewage Discharge Notifications'. Channels per alert.ny.gov/about: 'email, text messaging, phone, and fax'. No public RSS (alert.ny.gov/rss.xml is an empty Drupal channel), no public API, no public archive page. The legacy nyalert.gov host no longer resolves. Owner must subscribe (account creation not done by agent).
fields: same template as the DEC view (the DEC view is a copy of these messages)
cadence: push, as filed; law: 'as soon as possible but no later than four hours' after discovery to the public
license: NY-Alert website disclaimer only; no data licence
status_reason: Authoritative push channel; can be machine-ingested by parsing subscribed emails (template is fixed). Requires owner sign-up per county (62 counties).
notes: alert.ny.gov/about lists 'Sewage Discharge Notifications - Be informed when public waterways near you are impacted by untreated and partially treated sewage discharges'.

name: NYC DEP Waterbody Advisory System (dashboard JSON API)
access_detail: Angular dashboard linked from https://www.nyc.gov/site/dep/water/waterbody-advisories.page. Unauthenticated JSON endpoints found in the app bundle and fetched 2026-11-01: /api/profile (config: show_advisories 'wq'; wq layer waterbody_wq_advisory_staging; cso layer waterbody_csov2_advisory_staging), /api/advisory?advisoryType=WQ|CSO (45 rows: occurredOn, waterbody{id,name,class,rainGauge}, duration [hours], message, volume), /api/sensors (14 WRRF rain gauges with accumulatedLast24Hours), /api/rainfall-samples?page=N&pageSize=96&sensorId=CI (hourly rainfall, history back to at least Sept 2025), /api/calendar. The occurredOn parameter is ignored: /api/advisory returns only the current state.

valid_until (occurredOn + duration hours, computed by the app)
geometry (official affected area polygon via ArcGIS layer)

license: No licence stated on the app. NYC Terms of Use apply to nyc.gov content (not quoted).
status_reason: Real-time, polygon-based, model-driven advisories for 45 waterbodies; poll hourly and store. Not a discharge record; an official advisory.

name: ECL 17-0826-a, Sewage Pollution Right to Know Act (L.2012 c.368)
access_detail: Fetched nysenate.gov (current version dated 2014-09-22). Legislation API needs a key (401).
status_reason: Statutory deadlines and DEC duty to publish
notes: Quote (1): 'Publicly owned treatment works or the operator of a publicly owned sewer system shall immediately, but in no case later than two hours after discovery, report discharges of untreated or partially treated sewage, including combined sewer overflows, except partially treated sewage discharged directly from a publicly owned treatment works that is in compliance with a department approved plan or permit, to the department and the local health department...' Content (a)-(f): volume and treated state; date and time; expected duration; steps to contain 'except for wet weather combined sewer overflow discharges'; location 'with the maximum level of specificity possible'; reason. (2): 'as soon as possible, but no later than four hours from discovery of the discharge' notify local health department, chief elected official of the municipality and of 'any adjoining municipality that may be affected'; 'The same notification shall also be provided within the same timeframe to the general public ... through appropriate electronic media, including, but not limited to, electronic mail or voice communication as determined by the department.' (3): 'The department, in consultation with the department of health, shall post reported information on its website expeditiously and shall prepare a report on publicly owned treatment works and sewer system discharges annually.' (4): public notification regulations 'shall provide only for public notification of discharges that may present a threat to public health'.

name: 6 NYCRR 750-2.7 Incident reporting and notification requirements (amended eff. 2016-11-09)
access_detail: Fetched from Cornell LII (Justia returned 403). Note: 'Amended New York State Register November 9, 2016/Volume XXXVIII, Issue 45, eff. 11/9/2016'.
status_reason: Operational rules: electronic media, CSO waterbody advisories, daily/termination reports, 5-day written report
notes: (b)(2)(i): 'Immediately, but in no case later than two hours after discovery of the discharge, owners and operators of POTWs and POSSs must report all discharges of untreated or partially treated sewage, including combined sewer overflows, to the department and the local health department...' using 'appropriate electronic media as determined by the department'. (b)(2)(ii)(b): 'As soon as possible, but no later than four hours from discovery of the discharge, owners and operators of POTWs and POSSs must notify the general public...' (b)(2)(iii): 'For combined sewer overflows for which real-time telemetered discharge monitoring and detection does not exist, owners and operators ... must expeditiously issue advisories to the general public ... when, based on actual rainfall data or predictive models, enough rain has fallen that combined sewer overflows may discharge. Advisories may be done on a waterbody basis rather than by individual combined sewer overflow points.' (b)(2)(iv): daily reports 'for each day that the discharge continues' within 24 h of the previous report, termination report allowed; 'POTWs and POSSs are not required to file daily and termination reports for wet weather CSO events.' (d): five-day written report, not required 'for wet weather combined sewer overflows that are in compliance with a department approved plan or permit.' The regulation does not name NY-Alert; DEC designates it ('department approved form of electronic media'). Registration plus timely reports = compliance.

name: Matter of Riverkeeper, Inc. v NYC Dept. of Envtl. Protection, 2026 NY Slip Op 03444 (App Div 2d Dept, June 3, 2026)
access_detail: Decision page returned 403 to curl and WebFetch. Content from amNY (2026-06-04) and Inside Climate News (2026-08-05), both fetched. Lower court: Queens County Supreme Court, Nov 2023 (2023 NY Slip Op 23363).
status_reason: Appellate Division affirmed that DEP failed to give required SPRTK public notices; the city is petitioning the Court of Appeals (ICN 2026-08-05). Outcome may force per-discharge NYC notices.
notes: amNY: city argued its online list of overflow locations complied; court 'agreed with Riverkeeper that the law requires notification when a discharge starts.' ICN: NYC discharged an estimated 20.25 billion gallons of CSO in 2024 per DEC data; groups estimated at least 52 East River discharges in 2019 from five outfalls vs 11 advisories that year.
